newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals markets dull and slow.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals markets dull and slow.

text.p: The precious metals markets were lacklustre on Tuesday as prices kept to tight ranges due to a dearth of business ahead of the holidays.
"Everything's winding down for Christmas," a dealer said.
Bullion was fixed at $368.20 an ounce, barely changed from the morning's fixing of $368.30 or Monday afternoon's $368.25.
Dealers and analysts pegged gold's near term price range at $367-$370 an ounce.

Gyrations in the jittery equities markets were having little noticeable effect so far on the precious metals, as investors continued to stay away from gold. Stock markets eased following higher-than-expected U.S. housing starts data.
A potentially market-moving hike in interest rates by the U.S. central bank's Federal Open Markets Committee on Tuesday was also considered unlikely by analysts.
"It would take something extraordinary to move the gold market," a dealer said.
"By now 50-point movements on Wall Street are run of the mill. The only way gold would rise in these short market conditions is a move in interest rates," he added.
In terms of supply, South Africa's Chamber of Mines said gold output was likely to be around 490-495 tonnes this year, falling short of earlier industry forecasts of 500 tonnes.
Platinum, which came under pressure overnight when investors liquidated long positions in Tokyo, was likely to be more volatile in coming days, analysts said..
Prices were already at three-year lows and price charts suggested a slide to the $365 support level was possible in the near term, said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse.
Platinum was $0.50 firmer at $367.05/$368.05 an ounce, against Monday's weak London close.
"It's the one to watch because the trend is so bearish that there's a chance platinum could spike up on short covering," a dealer noted.
Its sister metal palladium, indicated at $117.25/$118.25 was unchanged from Monday's London close.
Silver, like gold, was virtually static and seen wedged in a tight range. It was indicated at $4.81/$4.83 an ounce, up two cents from the previous close.
